title: A TRIM15-CDX2 loop drives bile acid-induced gastric intestinal metaplasia.
authors: Wang, Dan; Chen, Jian; Xu, Wei; Shrestha, Sachin Mulmi; Lu, Qin; Ren, Lihua; Ji, Qinghua; Wu, Hailu; Shi, Ruihua
one_liner_zh: 该文研究胆汁酸诱导胃肠化生中TRIM15-CDX2调控环，涉及CDX2与TRIM15启动子结合（ChIP）及蛋白-蛋白对接，但核心是信号通路与疾病机制，非TF-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，仅部分相关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Gastric intestinal metaplasia (GIM), a precancerous lesion and risk factor for gastric cancer, is closely associated with chronic bile acid (BA) exposure; however, its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to identify key regulators involved in BA-associated GIM and to elucidate their functional roles. METHODS: TRIM15 and GIM markers (CDX2, MUC2, KLF4, and VIL1) were assessed in human GIM and paired normal tissues by RNA-seq, RT‒qPCR, Western blotting (WB), and immunofluorescence (IF). BA profiles were analyzed using UHPLC‒MS/MS. In vitro, GES-1 cells were treated with CDCA and subjected to TRIM15 gain- and loss-of-function assays. CDX2-mediated transcriptional regulation of TRIM15 was evaluated by dual-luciferase reporter and ChIP assays. NF-kappaB signaling and related proteins were assessed by WB and IF. The interaction between TRIM15 and IkappaBalpha and the levels of ubiquitination were investigated by coimmunoprecipitation, LC-MS/MS and protein-protein docking analysis. Functional assays were used to assess proliferation and apoptosis. In vivo validation was performed using an AAV9-mediated TRIM15 knockdown rat model. RESULTS: TRIM15 expression was consistently upregulated in GIM and increased stepwise with disease severity, accompanied by a positive association with CDX2 expression. BA profiling revealed the selective enrichment of cholic acid (CA) and chenodeoxycholic acid (CDCA), which induced GIM-associated phenotypes in vitro. Mechanistically, CDX2 directly bound to the TRIM15 promoter to increase its transcription, whereas TRIM15 promoted CDX2 expression via the NF-kappaB pathway, resulting in the formation of a regulatory loop. Further mechanistic analyses revealed that TRIM15 promoted K48-linked ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of IkappaBalpha, thereby enhancing p65 phosphorylation. Notably, this effect was abolished by expression of the degradation-resistant IkappaBalpha S32A/S36A mutant. In vivo, TRIM15 knockdown attenuated gastric mucosal injury and intestinal metaplasia and reduced NF-kappaB signaling and CDX2 expression. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest the involvement of a TRIM15-NF-kappaB-CDX2 regulatory loop in BA-associated GIM. TRIM15 may contribute to epithelial reprogramming under BA exposure and could be a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for GIM progression.
abstract_zh: 背景：胃黏膜肠上皮化生（GIM）是胃癌的癌前病变和危险因素，与慢性胆汁酸（BA）暴露密切相关；然而，其分子机制尚不清楚。本研究旨在识别参与BA相关GIM的关键调控因子，并阐明其功能作用。方法：通过RNA-seq、RT-qPCR、Western blotting（WB）和免疫荧光（IF）评估人GIM及配对正常组织中TRIM15和GIM标志物（CDX2、MUC2、KLF4和VIL1）的表达。使用UHPLC-MS/MS分析BA谱。体外实验中，用CDCA处理GES-1细胞，并进行TRIM15功能获得和功能丧失实验。通过双荧光素酶报告基因和ChIP实验评估CDX2对TRIM15的转录调控。通过WB和IF评估NF-kappaB信号通路及相关蛋白。通过免疫共沉淀、LC-MS/MS和蛋白质-蛋白质对接分析研究TRIM15与IkappaBalpha之间的相互作用及泛素化水平。使用功能实验评估增殖和凋亡。使用AAV9介导的TRIM15敲低大鼠模型进行体内验证。结果：TRIM15表达在GIM中持续上调，并随疾病严重程度逐步增加，且与CDX2表达呈正相关。BA谱分析显示胆酸（CA）和鹅去氧胆酸（CDCA）选择性富集，这些物质在体外诱导了GIM相关表型。机制上，CDX2直接结合TRIM15启动子以增加其转录，而TRIM15通过NF-kappaB通路促进CDX2表达，形成调控环路。进一步的机制分析揭示，TRIM15促进IkappaBalpha的K48连接泛素化及随后的蛋白酶体降解，从而增强p65磷酸化。值得注意的是，这种效应被抗降解的IkappaBalpha S32A/S36A突变体表达所消除。在体内，TRIM15敲低减轻了胃黏膜损伤和肠上皮化生，并降低了NF-kappaB信号通路和CDX2表达。结论：这些发现提示TRIM15-NF-kappaB-CDX2调控环路参与BA相关GIM。TRIM15可能在BA暴露下促进上皮重编程，并可能成为GIM进展的潜在生物标志物和治疗靶点。
